title: Ops sprint: launch pad tidy checklist + signal sampling notes (May 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working "launch pad tidy" checklist for our five-day ops sprint before the vNext rollout. Focus is on making the cutover low-friction: tidy infra cruft, ensure signal coverage, validate rollback gates, and draft the customer-facing release notes. Use this as the single source-of-truth for preflight owners and the on-call run sheet for the first 24h after cutover.

High-level goals:
- Reduce unknowns: limit launch surface to the smallest feature set that meets product acceptance.
- Verify observability: end-to-end traces, critical KPIs, and sampling points are in place.
- Fast rollback: decisions can be made in <30m with clear criteria.
- Clear comms: stakeholders know where to watch and how to escalate.

Owner matrix (who does what)
- Release lead: Marcus Nguyen (coordination, go/no-go)
- Telemetry lead: Priya Shah (dashboards + alert sanity)
- QA lead: Lina Ortega (smoke + canary test checklist)
- Infra lead: Ethan Park (deploy scripts, infra toggles)
- Release notes & comms: Product marketing (draft below)

Preflight tidy checklist (day -5 to day -1)
- [ ] Freeze non-essential changes in dependent services (cherry-pick policy in place).
- [ ] Dependency audit: confirm third-party SDK versions and feature flags.
- [ ] Cleanup stale config: remove deprecated feature flags or mark as guarded.
- [ ] Confirm canary cluster capacity: reserve 15% of production for canary traffic.
- [ ] Prepare smoke-run artifacts: docker image tags, migration rollbacks, DB read-only flags.
- [ ] Confirm secrets & KMS access for private deployments: rotate test keys and validate KMS policies.
- [ ] Validate CI artifact provenance: SHA checksums and signed releases for binaries.
- [ ] Update runbook pointers in Slack with short links and tag lists.

Launch-day timeline (local timezone UTC)
- T-60m: final go/no-go meeting (release lead + leads). Quick checklist: deployment window, pager roster, telemetry green, rollback plan present.
- T-30m: Lock traffic routing rules and start rolling preflight traffic to canary.
- T-15m: Run smoke tests against canary (see smoke checklist below).
- T+0: Begin staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 10-15m dwell between steps.
- T+1h: Validate stability signals, increase to next stage if no regression.
- T+24h: Post-launch retro sync (short) and hand back to product support.

Staged rollout policy (quick)
- Canary: internal + synthetic traffic only. Target: 5-10% of requests. Dwell: 15m with sampling.
- Gradual expansion: 10% increments with telemetry check at each step. Dwell: 10-30m depending on latency spike magnitude.
- Fallback: automatic re-route to prior model variant or previous binary if error ratio > threshold for 3 consecutive minutes.

Smoke & canary test checklist (automation + manual)
- Automated:
  - [ ] Happy-path generation test: sample prompt suite (10 prompts) with latency < SLA p95.
  - [ ] KV-cache warmup: ensure cache hit % > 60% for repeated prefix workload.
  - [ ] Embedding endpoint sanity: top-k similarity smoke queries.
  - [ ] Auth & quotas: verify token validation and rate limiter not rejecting legitimate test clients.
- Manual:
  - [ ] Run local end-to-end flow from SDK -> API -> response parsing.
  - [ ] Check stall scenarios: long-context generation for a small set to ensure memory/KV handling.
  - [ ] Run degradation test: inject 1% synthetic failures to observe graceful fallback.

Key telemetry signals to sample (and suggested queries)
- Error budget & SLOs: p99 latency, p95 latency, error rate (5xx), model token-generation errors.
  - Query snippet: "sum(rate(api_request_errors[5m])) / sum(rate(api_requests[5m]))" (PromQL)
- Resource pressure: GPU utilization by node, OOM events, model cache eviction rate.
  - Query snippet: "max_over_time(gpu_utilization[15m])"
- Quality regressions: top-k token shift or unexpected perplexity spikes (when we run eval sets).
- Customer impact: failed user-facing transactions, telemetry-tagged incidents from client SDKs.

Sampling plan (what to collect and why)
- Lightweight traces for 1000 requests/minute sampled across regions for 3 hours post-rollout to catch cross-region regressions.
- Full traces for 10% of errors for the first 6h to accelerate root cause.
- Aggregated prompt/response hash sampling (no PII) to detect content-level regressions.

Rollback decision matrix
- Immediate rollback triggers (auto):
  - Error rate > 2x baseline for 5m AND user-facing SLA broken.
  - GPU OOM rate spike > 1% across >10% nodes.
  - Data integrity confirmed failure (migration error, persistent store write failure).
- Manual rollback triggers (escalate):
  - Latency p95 > 3x baseline for 30m with customer tickets rising.
  - Quality regression detected on eval set (significant metric drop tied to model change).

Operations commands & artifacts (cheat sheet)
- Deploy: ./scripts/deploy --tag vNext --stages canary,10,50,100 --dwell 15m --owner @release-lead
- Canary rollback: ./scripts/rollback --to-tag vPrev --force --reason "error-rate-threshold"
- Health checks: curl -sS https://canary-api.redwood.internal/health | jq .status
- Telemetry quick checks (BigQuery):
  - "SELECT AVG(latency_ms) FROM api_logs WHERE tag='canary' AND timestamp > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 MINUTE)"

Comm plan (who says what, where)
- Pre-launch: #release-notifications Slack channel — release lead posts T-60m note with link to runbook.
- During launch: #release-ops pinned message updated at each stage. Pager rotations posted internally.
- Post-launch: short announcement to #product and #support with release notes link and known issues.

Sample release notes (draft for PM/marketing edit)
- Title: vNext: improved inference stability and optimized cost controls (May 2026)
- Short summary: This release reduces token-generation tail latency by ~20% for long-context workloads and introduces a new cache priming optimization for common prefixes.
- What's new:
  - Cache priming: reduces repeated-prefix token cost and latency.
  - Autoscaler tweaks: smoother scale-down behavior to reduce tail-latency spikes.
  - Security: rotated KMS keys for private deployments and tightened IAM rules.
- Known issues:
  - Rare model eviction may cause slightly higher cold-start latency for some very-long-sequence workloads (mitigation: increase canary dwell).
- Rollout plan: Canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full over 6h with telemetry gates at each stage.

Unresolved items / TODOs
- [ ] Confirm canary traffic generator script is configured to reproduce production distribution for embeddings. (Owner: Lina)
- [ ] Add a golden prompt set for long-context runs to telemetry (Owner: Priya).
- [ ] Finalize Max dwell time policy for region us-west1 (Owner: Ethan).
- [ ] PM to finalize customer-facing changelog headline by EOD before rollout.

Post-launch sampling and quick postmortem template
- Sampling windows: 0-3h (high frequency), 3-24h (medium), 24-72h (low).
- Quick postmortem template (fill within 48h):
  - Summary: short timeline of events and outcome.
  - Impact: user-visible effects and metrics (error-rate, latency delta).
  - Root cause(s): preliminary and confirmed.
  - Mitigation: what was done during rollout.
  - Long-term fixes: tracking tickets and owners.

Appendix: useful links & snippets
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/482
- Linear: https://linear.app/rel/issue/REL-312
- Runbook (confluence): confluence://pages/REL-678
- Slack: #release-ops (pin message for quick access)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc intentionally small; we don't need exhaustive runbooks for minor config flips. Aim for crisp fail-fast criteria.
- If a rollback occurs, capture exact telemetry windows (UTC) and include raw sampling hashes for later analysis.

If anyone reading this wants to add a short checklist item, push a one-line update here and tag the owner. We'll iterate quickly during the sprint.
